headline: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, a White House official told CBS News, after Axios first reported the departure. Cairncross, an attorney who has held the Senate confirmed role since August 2025, advised the president on cybersecurity and coordinated federal cyber strategy. His exit comes after a week of outages that hit Microsoft services, FAA air traffic control, major banks and an NSA internal network. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told lawmakers that investigators have seen nothing indicating the outages are related, and said he is “98% confident” they are not the result of malicious foreign activity. The reports do not link Cairncross’s departure to the outages and no official reason for his departure has been given.
